report.headline: Usage projected to fall to 14.1% in the NBA, below league average, while the true shooting projection carries no real information

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 14.1% in the NBA, down from 17.6% in the G League and below the NBA average of 20.1%.

risks.text: The true shooting projection of 52.5% is not trustworthy: the model's held-out error (4.7%) matches the error of a trivial league-mean baseline, so this number should not be used to evaluate the player.
The usage rate estimate is built from only 45 historical GL->NBA transitions, and its 80% interval (8.8% to 19.3%) still covers roughly two standard deviations of the NBA usage distribution.
The source-season sample is limited for a player already 27.0 years old, with 1,463 minutes across 50 games.

strengths.text: In the source season the subject posted a 56.4% true shooting mark, 0.19 SD above the G League average, built on a high share of attempts from three (53.1%).
Players who historically made this G League to NBA move sat about 0.27 SD above their league's average before moving, consistent with the subject's own standing.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 8.8% to 19.3%, a span of about 10.5 points against a league standard deviation of 5.2%, so the model can rank this player but not pin down his usage individually. The true shooting projection of 52.5% should not be read as informative: its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league average, which the bundle flags explicitly.
